rules.text: Damaged Stairs: The staircase requires some repairs based upon a visual inspection. Where loose handrails, damaged balustrades or uneven treads are present, these should be repaired promptly. Also, defective guarding should be repaired without delay.
Electrical Safety: Visible defects were identified. Further inspection by a qualified electrician is recommended before legal commitment.

Gas Safety: Gas appliances and installations were not assessed. Where there is any doubt regarding their age, condition or maintenance history, inspection by a Gas Safe registered engineer is recommended before legal commitment.

Asbestos: Properties constructed before 2000 may contain asbestos-containing materials (ACMs). As a precaution, we recommend that an asbestos identification survey is carried out by a suitably qualified and licensed asbestos surveyor before purchase, particularly if you intend to undertake refurbishment, alterations, or demolition works. In addition to any asbestos-containing materials specifically referred to elsewhere in this report, other concealed or inaccessible asbestos materials may also be present. The inspection undertaken for this survey is not intended to identify or confirm the presence of asbestos. According to the Health and Safety Executive (HSE), asbestos-containing materials do not normally present a significant health risk if they are in good condition and remain undisturbed. However, if such materials are damaged, drilled, cut, or otherwise disturbed, asbestos fibres may be released, posing a health hazard and requiring specialist management or removal. Any work involving suspected asbestos-containing materials must comply with the **Control of Asbestos Regulations 2012**. These regulations impose strict requirements on the assessment, handling, removal, and disposal of asbestos, which can significantly increase the cost of repair, maintenance, or alteration works. If asbestos is suspected or confirmed, your legal adviser should make appropriate enquiries regarding any previous asbestos surveys, removal works, or management records relating to the property. Further advice should be obtained where refurbishment is proposed.
Mould Growth: Localised mould growth associated with condensation was observed. Maintaining adequate heating and ventilation should assist in reducing further mould growth.

General Advice: The inspection identified matters requiring repair, maintenance, or further investigation. These should be considered before legal commitment and reflected in your future maintenance planning. Buildings require regular inspection and maintenance throughout their service life. Prompt attention to isolated defects will normally reduce the likelihood of more extensive deterioration and costly future repairs. Where specialist inspections have been recommended within this report, these should be obtained before legal commitment where practicable.
